summary:
Mission Health is a website we created to help astronauts monitor their health and recognize possible health concerns during space missions. Living in space can affect the human body in many ways, including changes in heart health, sleep patterns, and mental well-being. Since astronauts may be far from Earth, having an easy way to track these changes is important.

Our website allows astronauts to enter daily health information such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, and exercise. Based on these measurements, the dashboard uses green, yellow, and red indicators to show whether a reading may need attention. We also included graphs to track changes over time, an interactive body map that highlights areas of concern, and a feature that connects reported symptoms to related health measurements.

Our goal was to make health information easier for astronauts to understand without needing to interpret complicated data themselves. Mission Health addresses the challenge by bringing different health measurements together in one place, helping astronauts notice potential problems earlier and make more informed decisions about their health during long missions.
details:
Github repository link: https://github.com/bilaltalukder/space-apps-health-monitoring.git

Mission Health is a website our team developed to help astronauts monitor their health and recognize possible health concerns during space missions. Living in space can affect the human body in many ways, including changes in cardiovascular health, sleep patterns, and mental wellness Since astronauts may be far with limited access to medical assistance, we wanted to create a tool that makes tracking their health easier and more understandable.

Our website allows astronauts to enter daily health measurements, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, and exercise. The system compares these measurements with reference ranges and uses green, yellow, and red indicators to show whether a reading is within the expected range or may require attention. We also included graphs that track measurements over time, allowing astronauts to notice gradual changes that might otherwise go unnoticed.

One of our main features is the interactive human body map, which highlights different areas of the body depending on the health concerns detected. We also developed a symptom detection feature that allows astronauts to describe how they are feeling during their daily check-in. The system identifies relevant symptoms and connects them to related health measurements. These features help astronauts better understand how their symptoms and measurements might be connected.

To develop Mission Health, our team used HTML to structure the website, CSS for design and JavaScript to program the interactive features and health monitoring system. We used Visual Studio Code to write and test our code, GitHub and GitHub Desktop to collaborate and manage changes, and GitHub Pages to publish the website online.
